1. "He who has a why to live can bear almost any how." — Friedrich Nietzsche, *Twilight of the Idols*

2. "What does not kill me makes me stronger." — Friedrich Nietzsche, *Twilight of the Idols*

3. "No one can build you the bridge on which you, and only you, must cross the river of life." — Friedrich Nietzsche, *Schopenhauer as Educator*

4. "The surest way to corrupt a youth is to instruct him to hold in higher esteem those who think alike than those who think differently." — Friedrich Nietzsche, *The Dawn*

5. "Man is condemned to be free; because once thrown into the world, he is responsible for everything he does." — Jean-Paul Sartre, *Existentialism Is a Humanism*

6. "In the midst of winter, I finally learned that there was in me an invincible summer." — Albert Camus, *Return to Tipasa*

7. "Man is the only creature who refuses to be what he is." — Albert Camus, *The Rebel*

8. "The unexamined life is not worth living." — Socrates, in Plato's *Apology*

9. "Wonder is the beginning of philosophy." — Plato, *Theaetetus*

10. "The beginning is the most important part of the work." — Plato, *Republic*

11. "All men by nature desire to know." — Aristotle, *Metaphysics*

12. "Man is by nature a political animal." — Aristotle, *Politics*

13. "We suffer more often in imagination than in reality." — Seneca, *Letters to Lucilius*

14. "It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it." — Seneca, *On the Shortness of Life*

15. "Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of them." — Epictetus, *Enchiridion*

16. "First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do." — Epictetus, *Discourses*

17. "The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way." — Marcus Aurelius, *Meditations*

19. "The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts." — Marcus Aurelius, *Meditations*

20. "Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains." — Jean-Jacques Rousseau, *The Social Contract*

21. "I think, therefore I am." — René Descartes, *Discourse on Method*

22. "The life of man is solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short." — Thomas Hobbes, *Leviathan*

23. "Life can only be understood backwards; but it must be lived forwards." — Søren Kierkegaard, *Journals*

24. "Anxiety is the dizziness of freedom." — Søren Kierkegaard, *The Concept of Anxiety*

25. "Talent hits a target no one else can hit; genius hits a target no one else can see." — Arthur Schopenhauer, *The World as Will and Representation*

26. "The philosophers have only interpreted the world in various ways; the point, however, is to change it." — Karl Marx, *Theses on Feuerbach*

27. "Sapere aude! Have courage to use your own understanding!" — Immanuel Kant, *What Is Enlightenment?*

28. "The good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge." — Bertrand Russell, *What I Believe*

29. "The limits of my language mean the limits of my world." — Ludwig Wittgenstein, *Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus*

30. "Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom. Mastering others is strength; mastering yourself is true power." — Lao Tzu, *Tao Te Ching*
